Opc.Ua.SpecificationPublisher — build an OPC UA companion specification from markdown.

  build [--manifest spec.json] [--out _work/artifacts]
        markdown + NodeSet -> NISO STS 1.2 Extended XML

  publish [--in _work/artifacts] [--out _work/docs] [--site-url <url>]
        STS -> the browsable specification. One HTML page:
        numbered clauses, real tables, figures, and every
        cross-reference resolved. That is the artifact an author
        reviews - the markdown source carries no numbering and the
        STS is not for reading.

        Renders the XML rather than the document the build had in
        memory, on purpose. The STS is what every downstream
        rendering comes from, so reading it back makes the page a
        standing check on it: whatever the STS failed to carry is
        visibly missing here.

        The output directory is served as-is, so it is what Pages
        publishes from a branch folder - point Pages at main /docs.

        A README.md is written there too, because GitHub renders one
        when anyone opens the folder and what they would otherwise
        find is unreadable generated HTML. --site-url puts a link to
        the published page in it; a private Pages site has a
        randomised hostname that cannot be derived, so the workflow
        reads it with the token it already has and passes it here.

  word [--in _work/artifacts] [--out _work/artifacts]
        STS -> the Word edition. Renders into the base template,
        which carries the cover, the running heads, the Contents,
        Figures and Tables fields and the IEC style set, and ships
        inside this tool - so every working group's document is
        built from the same one.

        Numbering is Word's, not the build's: clause numbers, "Annex
        A", table and figure numbers and every cross-reference are
        fields, so a person who inserts a clause in the generated
        document gets a correctly renumbered one. What the STS says
        those numbers should be is checked again
[truncated]
